Phonosemantic compound. 木 represents the meaning and 尌 represents the sound.
生植之緫名。从木尌聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *djoʔ, *djos): semantic 木 (“tree”) + phonetic 尌 (OC *djos, “to plant a tree”). Originally written as 尌; an extra 木 was added to differentiate.
Area word (Schuessler, 2007): Mizo tuh (“to plant, to sow”), Khmer ដុះ (doh, “to grow, to bud”). Starostin compares it with Tibetan གདོས (gdos), གདོས་པ (gdos pa, “mast”) and Burmese ထူ (htu, “to erect (a post), to raise (a flag)”).
Related to 豎 (OC *djoʔ, “to erect; to make vertical”).

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: For 樹, the dictionary gives the Shuowen account 生植之總名。从木，尌聲 (“general name for growing plants; from 木, with 尌 as phonetic”). It records the tree sense, planting/cultivating, and establishing, with examples from the Shiji, Mengzi, Liji, and Shangshu. These are dictionary-attested senses; the page does not date the first occurrence of each sense.
evidence.title: [A02024] 樹 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 尌 字形及形義源流
evidence.text: This account identifies an oracle-bone form of 尌 as a tree graph with 又 (hand), interpreting it as planting a tree and ‘setting upright’; it calls 尌 an early form of 樹. It separately reports that bronze forms added 豆 as a phonetic element and that graphic change produced a 壴-like form, after which 木 was added to 樹. This is a scholarly account of graphic development, not an uncontested description of the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 裘錫圭, 釋「尌」, Fudan University Center for the Study of Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: discussion of 樹 and 尌 graph history
evidence.text: Qiu argues that 樹 and 尌 were originally one graph/word for ‘plant/set upright’; on his account a form with 木 underwent graphic changes, including corruption toward 壴 and 寸, and 木 was later added to distinguish 樹. He discusses competing explanations and rejects an alternative ‘candle’ interpretation as insufficiently supported. This conflicts in detail with accounts that treat the components as a straightforward semantic 木 plus phonetic 尌 from the outset.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：釋「尌」

evidence.source: 說文解字在線查詢 Shuowen.org
evidence.field: 樹 entry and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The page reproduces the Shuowen entry 樹, 生植之緫名。从木尌聲, and identifies a 籀文 form. Duan Yucai’s note says 植 can mean 立 and be borrowed for 尌/豎; it also interprets the graph as phonetic with a possible associative aspect. This is a historical lexicographic analysis, not direct evidence for the date of the first tree or planting sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「樹」

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No primary inscription image was visually inspected. The discussion of oracle-bone and bronze forms is reported from specialist textual accounts only.

Sources disagree about the internal graphic history of 尌: a hand planting a tree analysis versus a 豆/壴-related sound element and subsequent corruption/addition of 木. The sources support the disagreement but do not resolve it conclusively.

The sound component’s own historical reconstruction was not present in the supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows, and an independently verified 尌 reading was not found here. Shuowen labels 尌 phonetic, but a same-system historical sound comparison remains a gap.

No securely dated earliest attestation was established for 樹 specifically meaning ‘tree’ versus the verbal senses ‘plant/set upright’; Shuowen is a Han lexicographic record, not a date for the word’s first use. Later dictionary citations include Shiji/Mengzi/Shangshu examples but do not establish chronology from gloss order.
The requested official Unihan character pages for U+6811 and U+6A39 failed to open in the browser. Local kMandarin rows are reported as local data, not as verified external page contents.
No bulk reuse terms were checked; the findings use short paraphrases of character-specific and scholarly pages, so no tracked extract is recommended.
The Fudan article was returned as a search result but its page timed out on open; its detailed competing analysis therefore remains only partially verified in this run.

The direct Wikimedia Commons description page for 尌-seal.svg returned a cache miss; no exact file description, license, original-image URL, or image provenance could be verified. No glyph candidate is proposed.

The Xiaoxuetang character query did not yield an exact 樹 form record or direct glyph asset in this run. The general database homepage is not sufficient image provenance; chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw states All Rights Reserved and was not used as an image source.

No directly inspected primary inscription image or securely dated earliest attestation of 樹 for the noun ‘tree’ versus verbal senses was established. The MOE entry cites classical works for separate uses but its gloss/example order does not establish chronology.

The familiar Shuowen component account labels 尌 phonetic and 木 semantic; Qiu’s alternative graph-history account was only partially visible through search-result text. The exact early shape history and whether the relation began as a phonetic compound remain disputed.

The local Baxter–Sagart readings are consistent for 尌 and two 樹 readings in MC/OC notation, but no official Unicode per-character reading page was successfully inspected in this run. Local rows are not external page verification.

limitations.text: No glyph illustration is available here to show the relevant forms: 樹 is analyzed in the Shuowen account as 木 with 尌 phonetic, but no directly inspected, character-specific historical glyph image is established. The early graphic history of 尌 and its relation to 樹 also remains disputed.
